Chevron completed its acquisition of Hess Corporation on July 18, 2025, with an aggregate purchase price of approximately $48 billion [1][2].
As part of the transaction, Chevron assumed debt with an aggregate outstanding principal value of $8.8 billion [2].
Hess operates as an independent oil and gas exploration and production company with principal upstream operations in the United States, Guyana, and Malaysia, along with an approximately 38 percent ownership interest in Hess Midstream LP [2][3].
Chevron notes that the success of the acquisition depends on realizing anticipated benefits such as cost synergies, production and free cash flow growth rates, and long-term returns to shareholders [4].
Additionally, Chevron points out that the acquisition may cause financial results to differ from expectations, disrupt current operations, or face operational challenges and unforeseen expenses [4].

citations.quote: The acquisition of Hess Corporation (Hess) was completed on July 18, 2025.

The aggregate purchase price of Hess was approximately $48 billion, including 15.38 million shares of Hess common stock purchased in open market transactions in the first quarter of 2025 and 301.25 million shares of Chevron common stock issued as closing consideration in July. As part of the transaction, the company assumed debt with an aggregate outstanding principal value of $8.8 billion.

On July 18, 2025, the company acquired Hess Corporation (Hess), an independent oil and gas exploration and production company. Hess’s principal upstream operations are in the United States, Guyana and Malaysia. Hess’s operations also include an approximately 38 percent ownership interest in Hess Midstream LP (HESM), with operations primarily in the Bakken shale in the Williston Basin area of North Dakota.

The acquisition of Hess may cause Chevron’s financial results to differ from the company’s expectations or the expectations of the investment community, the company may not achieve the anticipated benefits of the acquisition, and the acquisition may disrupt the company’s current plans or operations The success of the acquisition of Hess, which closed in July 2025, will depend, in part, on Chevron’s ability to realize the anticipated benefits, including the anticipated run-rate cost synergies, estimated five-year production and free cash flow growth rates, and anticipated higher returns to shareholders over the long-term.

answer.answer: Prologis partners with many of the world's largest institutional investors through co-investment ventures as part of its strategic capital business [1]. The business is capitalized through private and public equity, consisting of 94% open-ended ventures, long-term ventures, and three publicly traded vehicles [1]. These three publicly traded vehicles are Nippon Prologis REIT, Inc. in Japan, China AMC Prologis Logistics REIT in China, and FIBRA Prologis in Mexico [1]. Prologis aligns its interests with its partners by holding significant ownership interests in these co-investment ventures [1]. Management of the unconsolidated co-investment ventures comprises the Strategic Capital Segment [1].

citations.quote: We partner with many of the world’s largest institutional investors through co-investment ventures. The business is capitalized through private and public equity, and is comprised of 94% open-ended ventures, long-term ventures and three publicly traded vehicles: (i) Nippon Prologis REIT, Inc. in Japan; (ii) China AMC Prologis Logistics REIT in China; and (iii) FIBRA Prologis in Mexico (which controls and owns more than 99% of Terrafina, also a publicly traded FIBRA). We align our interests with our partners by holding significant ownership interests in the co-investment ventures. Ten of the co-investment ventures are unconsolidated entities, and one is consolidated, with our ownership in the co-investment ventures ranging from 15% to 55%. This structure allows us to reduce our exposure to foreign currency fluctuations for non-U.S. investments. Management of the unconsolidated co-investment ventures comprises our Strategic Capital Segment.
